ops.text: Go's internal/realhome honours the DAEMONKIT_HOME env override in production (with a logged warning), and Swift's RealHome.directory() does not — it reads getpwuid(getuid()) unconditionally. Both halves therefore agree on the home only when nothing sets the override. A consumer split across both languages, captain-hook being the one that exists, would have its Go daemon bind a socket under the override while its Swift client dials one under the passwd home: two different paths, no error, a connect that just never finds anything. Found while adding AgentPaths in v0.23.0. The new paths/testdata/agent-layout.json golden pins the layout formula on both sides but takes the home as an input, so it cannot catch this axis. Left alone deliberately: teaching Swift the override is a production behaviour change well outside a path-shortening release.
